import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/cameras.csv')

# Set a professional style for the plot
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid")

# Create the scatter plot
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 8))
sns.scatterplot(
    data=df,
    x='megapixels',
    y='price_usd',
    hue='sensor_type',      # Differentiate by sensor type
    style='body_type',      # Differentiate by body type
    size='weight_grams',    # Represent weight with point size
    sizes=(50, 800),        # Range for point sizes
    alpha=0.7,              # Add transparency to handle overplotting
    palette='viridis'       # Choose a color palette
)

# Apply a logarithmic scale to the y-axis (price) for better visualization of skewed data
plt.yscale('log')

# Set title and labels
plt.title('Camera Price vs. Megapixels by Sensor Type and Body Type', fontsize=16, pad=20)
plt.xlabel('Megapixels', fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel('Price (USD, Log Scale)', fontsize=12)

# Customize the legend
# Combine hue and style legends for clarity. Seaborn usually handles this well.
# Place the legend outside the plot area to prevent obscuring data
plt.legend(title='Camera Attributes', bbox_to_anchor=(1.05, 1), loc='upper left', borderaxespad=0.)

# Improve layout
plt.tight_layout()

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
